title: 1 Samuel 13
paragraphs: ¹ Saul was thirty years old when he became king, and he reigned over Israel for forty-two years. ² Saul chose three thousand men from Israel; two thousand were with him at Michmash and in the hill country of Bethel, and a thousand were with Jonathan at Gibeah in Benjamin. The rest of the men he sent back home. ³ Jonathan attacked the Philistine outpost at Geba, and the Philistines heard about it. Saul had the trumpet blown throughout the land, saying, "Let the Hebrews hear!" ⁴ And all Israel heard the news: "Saul has attacked the Philistine outpost, and now Israel has become obnoxious to the Philistines." The people were summoned to join Saul at Gilgal. ⁵ The Philistines assembled to fight Israel, with three thousand chariots, six thousand charioteers, and soldiers as numerous as the sand on the seashore. They came up and camped at Michmash, east of Beth-aven.

⁶ When the Israelites saw that their situation was desperate and that their army was hard pressed, they hid in caves, thickets, rocks, pits, and cisterns. ⁷ Some Hebrews even crossed the Jordan to the land of Gad and Gilead. Saul remained at Gilgal, and all the troops with him were shaking with fear. ⁸ He waited seven days, the time set by Samuel; but Samuel did not come to Gilgal, and Saul's men began to scatter. ⁹ So Saul said, "Bring me the burnt offering and the fellowship offerings." And he offered up the burnt offering. ¹⁰ Just as he finished making the offering, Samuel arrived. Saul went out to greet him.

¹¹ "What have you done?" asked Samuel. Saul replied, "When I saw that the men were scattering away from me and that you did not come at the set time, and that the Philistines were assembling at Michmash, ¹² I thought, 'Now the Philistines will come down against me at Gilgal, and I have not sought the LORD's favor.' So I felt compelled to offer the burnt offering myself." ¹³ "You have done a foolish thing," Samuel said. "You have not kept the command the LORD your God gave you; if you had, he would have established your kingdom over Israel for all time. ¹⁴ But now your kingdom will not endure; the LORD has sought out a man after his own heart and appointed him ruler of his people, because you have not kept the LORD's command." ¹⁵ Then Samuel left Gilgal and went up to Gibeah in Benjamin, and Saul counted the men who were with him. There were about six hundred.

¹⁶ Saul and his son Jonathan, along with the men with them, stayed at Gibeah in Benjamin, while the Philistines were encamped at Michmash. ¹⁷ Raiding parties went out from the Philistine camp in three groups: one turned toward Ophrah in the vicinity of Shual, ¹⁸ another turned toward Beth-horon, and a third turned toward the borderland that looks over the valley of Zeboim toward the wilderness. ¹⁹ Not a blacksmith could be found in the whole land of Israel, because the Philistines had said, "Otherwise the Hebrews will make swords or spears!" ²⁰ So all the Israelites had to go down to the Philistines to sharpen their plowshares, mattocks, axes, and sickles.

²¹ The price was two-thirds of a shekel for sharpening plowshares and mattocks, and a third of a shekel for sharpening forks, axes, and for repointing goads. ²² So on the day of battle there was not a sword or spear in the hands of any of the troops with Saul and Jonathan; only Saul and his son Jonathan had weapons. ²³ Now a detachment of Philistines had gone out to the pass at Michmash.
